# nullplatform_workflow (Resource)

Manages a workflow of the workflow engine: its record (name, folder, owner) and its definition. Every change of `definition` saves a new revision; `revision` is the latest one, which a `nullplatform_workflow_alias` publishes.

~> **Note:** The resource owns the whole workflow. A revision saved outside Terraform (a draft in the editor, a publish from elsewhere) is drift: the plan shows it, and the next apply saves the configured definition as a new revision. Destroying the resource deletes the workflow with every revision; it fails while an alias of it is active.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nullplatform = {
      source = "nullplatform/nullplatform"
    }
  }
}

provider "nullplatform" {}

# The definition comes from a YAML file. Every change of it saves a new
# revision; the record's fields (name, key, description, path) are attributes,
# never written inside the definition.
resource "nullplatform_workflow" "release_notify" {
  name        = "release-notify"
  key         = "release-notify"
  path        = "/governance/releases"
  description = "Announces each release"

  definition = jsonencode(yamldecode(file("${path.module}/workflows/release-notify.yaml")))
}

# The same, with the definition written inline. Without a key the workflow is
# addressed by its id.
resource "nullplatform_workflow" "payments_gate" {
  name        = "payments-gate"
  description = "Logs a call to its webhook"

  definition = jsonencode({
    steps = {
      start = {
        id         = "start"
        name       = "On call"
        pluginType = "webhook"
        config     = { path = "/payments-gate", mode = "start" }
      }
      say = {
        id         = "say"
        name       = "Say"
        pluginType = "log"
        config     = { message = "called" }
      }
    }
    connections = [{ id = "c1", from = "start", to = "say" }]
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `definition` (String) The workflow's definition as a JSON object, usually `jsonencode(yamldecode(file(...)))`: `steps` (a map of step id to step, each with its `pluginType` and `config`), `connections`, and any other section the engine takes (`inputs`, `variables`, `outputs`, `execution`, `metadata`, `semanticVersion`, ...). It goes as written. The record's fields are attributes, so `name`, `key`, `description`, `path` and `nrn` are refused inside it, and so are `id`, `triggers` and `pinnedDescriptors`, which the API derives. Changing it saves a new revision; key order, spacing and a step `type` the API fills in are not a change.
- `name` (String) The workflow's name. Changing it renames the workflow in place; every revision saved after carries the new name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description of the workflow. Changing it saves no revision.
- `key` (String) A stable handle chosen by you, unique in the organization: a lowercase slug of at most 63 characters. The API never changes it, so changing it, setting it or removing it replaces the workflow (a new id, new webhook URLs). Leave it unset for a workflow that has none.
- `nrn` (String) The NRN that owns the workflow: who sees and edits it. When unset the API sets the organization's. Changing it moves the workflow.
- `path` (String) The folder the workflow is listed in, such as `/governance/releases`: a leading `/`, segments joined by one `/`, no trailing `/`. When unset the folder is left as it is. Changing it saves no revision.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `revision` (Number) The number of the latest revision, as the API reports it. It changes with every change of `definition`; an alias that takes it publishes each one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# A workflow can be imported by its id or by its key. Either way the state keeps the id.
terraform import nullplatform_workflow.release_notify wf_0123456789abcdef
terraform import nullplatform_workflow.release_notify release-notify
```
